subject: Request: Dataflow carveout and visibility exception — Zenith Health
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@zenith-health.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Zenith Health Procurement <procurement@zenith-health.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data locality / audit log carveout ask for DPA

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Zenith is excited to move forward. Procurement asked us to surface one blocking item on the DPA before they can sign: a clause on telemetry and subprocessor audit access. Specifically they want:

- Confirmation that telemetry (inference traces + KV-cache metadata) originating from Zenith customers in the US will not be exported outside the US without an explicit addendum.
- An audit-log access commitment for subprocessors that handle telemetry: the customer expects evidence of certifications or an on-demand audit report.

They attached a redline request (we've reproduced the key asks as comments) and asked whether Redwood can accept an exception or provide a technical control to limit export for this account.

Can you point me at who on your side owns data use carveouts and whether Product/Security can do a rapid review? We have an internal timeline (procurement would like signoff by EOD Thursday).

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Head of Integrations — Zenith Health

[attachment: Zenith_DPA_redline_v2.docx]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. I can take point on coordination. Quick notes:

- We need a product decision on whether we can support a per-account export-lock or a contractual carveout that limits telemetry export.
- Security will need to provide the list of subprocessors that see telemetry and whether they can provide audit artifacts (SOC2 + on-demand audit language).

Looping in Vivek (Security) and Laura (Product) to scope the technical feasibility and the risk/controls. Vivek/Laura — can you review the attached redline and confirm whether this is something we can commit to, or whether we should propose compensating controls (e.g., local routing to a US-only region + masking of KV keys)? Zenith has asked for EOD Thu — can we target an internal alignment by Wed EOD so I can respond?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Data locality / audit log carveout ask for DPA

Tessa / team — reviewed the redline and Zenith's asks. Summary of technical & risk posture:

- What they asked for: a contractual statement that telemetry will not leave the US for Zenith customers unless an addendum is signed; plus on-demand subprocessor audit evidence.
- Current platform: telemetry routing is region-aware, but we have cross-region replication for backups/telemetry analytics in certain internal pipelines. We do not currently offer a per-account hard export-lock.

Options to offer (ranked):
1) Per-account routing + data residency configuration (engineering effort; ETA ~6 weeks with prioritization; can be delivered as a dedicated region pin for Zenith).
2) Compensating controls: US-only routing for all production inference + KV masking + written operational attestations about subprocessor access (faster; legal-friendly).
3) Contractual carveout with an explicit exception requiring security review for any export, plus quarterly attestations from subprocessors (legal risk: weaker enforcement if we cannot physically prevent export).

Regarding subprocessors: we can provide the list and SOC2 reports for the vendors that ingest telemetry (their names plus certs). For on-demand audits, we typically negotiate limited-scope audit rights — full supplier audits are rare and operationally heavy.

I attached suggested redline language (inline comments) and flagged the specific clauses that require Product signoff on feasibility and Engineering prioritization. If Product opts for option 1 we need to triage into the roadmap immediately. If Product prefers option 2/3, Security will prepare the attestation package and a subprocessor evidence list.

Attachment: Zenith_DPA_redline_v2.docx (I left inline comments)

-Vivek
Principal Security Engineer

> On Mon, May 10, 2027 at 10:03 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. I can take point on coordination...

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@zenith-health.com>, Zenith Health Procurement <procurement@zenith-health.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Data locality / audit log carveout ask for DPA — proposed path forward

Hi Laura / Grace — following Vivek's assessment, proposed path for internal decision and external response: 

1) Product decision point: do we commit to building per-account export locks (Option 1) for Zenith? If yes, product needs to confirm prioritization (6-week delivery estimate) and whether we can offer a time-limited SLA.
2) If Product does NOT want to commit to Option 1, propose Option 2 to Zenith: US-only routing + KV masking + security attestation + list of subprocessors and SOC2 reports. This is achievable immediately but is a contractual compromise.
3) Legal / Sales: If we go Option 2, procurement will probably insist on quarterly attestations and that may need an addendum for audit rights. Security to confirm acceptable phrasing.

Ask: Laura — can you confirm whether Product can triage a 6-week scoped deliverable if we prioritize? If not, say so and we'll package Option 2. Grace/Vivek — please draft the attestation language and gather subprocessor evidence by Wed EOD so I can reply to Zenith with a formal option set.

Target external reply: Wed 17:00 PT. Zenith asked for Thu EOD but we should give them a clear, feasible option set earlier.

Thanks — I'll hold judgement until I hear from you.

Tessa
Director, Strategic Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Thanks,
Alex
